newsitem.title: USA: Safety 1st sees unexpectly high 1996 loss.
newsitem.headline: Safety 1st sees unexpectly high 1996 loss.

text.p: Safety 1st Inc said Thursday it expected unexpectedly high net losses for the fourth quarter and fiscal year ended Dec 31.

The company, a developer and distributor of child care products, said it expects lower than expected sales for the fourth quarter -- due in part to a product realignment program and delay of shipments until the first quarter of 1997.
It said it expects to report sales in the fourth quarter below the previously announced range of $24 million to $26 million, adding it expects to release results by March 5.

It said its expected losses were "compounded by an increase in the valuation of adjustment for asset impairment related to discontinued items, increases in other reserves and accruals" and a rise in selling and administrative expenses.

In the previous fourth quarter ended Dec 31, 1995, the company said it reported sales of $22.3 million and a net loss of $2.5 million, or $0.35 a share. In fiscal year 1995, net income was $3.2 million, or $0.45 a share, it said.
The company said it continues to work with Goldman, Sachs & Co to explore various alternatives to enhance shareholder value.
